gbm_population_evidence.quote: Participants must have histologically or cytologically confirmed WHO grade 4 glioma (including tumors with molecularly defined grade 4 astrocytoma)

candidate_evidence.quote: Sitagliptin is an investigational drug for this condition that works by inhibiting an enzyme called dipeptidyl peptidase 4 (DPP-4)

target_engagement_planned_evidence.quote: Difference in tumor CD8+ T cell count between the participants randomized to pre-surgical sitagliptin versus the participants randomized to no pre-surgical treatment.

role_evidence.quote: While sitagliptin is FDA-approved for diabetes treatment, its use in glioblastoma is investigational (experimental).

agents.stated_antitumour_mechanism: inhibiting an enzyme called dipeptidyl peptidase 4 (DPP-4), which MDSCs rely on to enter the brain and function
arms: Group 1: Presurgical and post surgical treatment with sitagliptin
Group 2: Post surgical treatment with sitagliptin

coder_notes: Post-operative chemotherapy is unnamed and not a registered intervention, so not listed as an agent; regimen coded combination because the description says all patients receive sitagliptin and chemotherapy. Group 2 (no presurgical treatment) works as the comparator for the primary outcome though both groups are registered EXPERIMENTAL. Eligibility allows grade 4 glioma including molecularly defined grade 4 astrocytoma with no IDH requirement; cns5_terminology coded historical per the grade 4 glioma rule, though 'molecularly defined' hints at CNS5 usage.
